schema_name: Kibookal Creature-Maker Magazine — Consolidated Backbone v2
purpose: Single-file consolidated backbone fusing all 9 system files. Drop this ONE file into the Magazine tab and the whole system loads.

system_manifest.core_premise: Ordinary objects are only ordinary until someone stares at them strangely.
system_manifest.primary_goal: Help children learn to see, imagine, combine, and make first versions without worrying about perfect drawing.

mindset: old enough to dislike babyish worksheets
interested in secrets, codes, cases, creatures, notebooks, odd facts and strange inventions

learning_intent.surface_activity: Turn an ordinary object into an object-creature using strange attachments.

system_manifest.fixed_system_rule: Each page shows one solved case and leaves one unsolved case for the child.
system_manifest.rotating_system_rule: Each page has a different Today's Strange Switch: the tiny feature that changes the object-creature's personality, movement, mood, or story.
important_constraints: Do not make eyes the repeated default Strange Switch.
The original object must remain visible inside the final creature.
The page must feel like a found secret notebook, not a worksheet.
The solved case teaches by example; the unsolved case invites participation.
Humour should be odd, dry, clever, and slightly mischievous.
The child should feel permission to make a first version, not pressure to make a masterpiece.

Reusable prompts, page-generation inputs, and negative prompts.
Checklist and scoring rubric for deciding whether a generated page works.

strange_switch_library.definition: A Strange Switch is the tiny feature that changes an object's personality, movement, mood, story, behaviour, danger, usefulness, or creature logic.
strange_switch_library.core_rule: Do not make the Strange Switch only a placement exercise. It should create different consequences: movement, behaviour, attitude, powers, problems, secrets, mistakes, or jokes.
strange_switch_library.anti_repetition_rule: Avoid five variations that all mean 'this part becomes a body part.' Each Strange Switch should include a mix of body change, behaviour change, story change, power change, and problem change.
selection_rules: Choose a feature that is either already present in the object or funny when attached to it.
The feature must create 4-7 interesting micro-experiments.
At least three micro-experiments should change behaviour or story, not just silhouette.
The feature should feel specific to the case, not generic.
If the previous page used eyes, the next page must not use eyes.
If a feature starts feeling decorative, make it cause trouble.

switches.principle: Eyes do not just make things alive. They decide what the creature notices, ignores, suspects, wants, or refuses to admit.
switches.avoid: Do not make every eye variation only an expression. Make some eyes change behaviour or story.

switches.principle: Fingers make an object look like it is about to touch, steal, point, count, crawl, accuse, or perform a very small crime.
switches.avoid: Do not make every finger variation just 'more fingers.' Make the fingers do different things.

switches.principle: Hair gives an object age, weather, ego, panic, style, disguise, or evidence that something exploded nearby.
switches.avoid: Do not make hair only decorative. Hair should reveal mood, history, or trouble.

switches.principle: A plug gives the creature power, dependence, danger, interruption, charging rituals, and questionable life choices.
switches.avoid: Do not make every plug a tail. Make it change power, limits, habits, and risks.

switches.principle: A clip grabs, hooks, hides, pins, listens, traps, carries, and pretends to be useful while causing trouble.
switches.avoid: Do not make every clip a fin, wing, arm, crest, or tail. Make the clip change what the creature does.

switches.principle: A zipper can be a mouth, border, spine, trap, secret door, warning line, or the sound of something about to happen.
switches.avoid: Do not make every zipper just teeth. Let it open, close, hide, warn, divide, or release things.

switches.principle: Wheels change speed, balance, escape plans, confidence, direction, and the number of apologies required afterward.
switches.avoid: Do not make every wheel variation just movement. Include control, dizziness, status, accidents, and escape.

switches.principle: Leaves bring disguise, forest gossip, seasonal mood swings, photosynthesis excuses, and the possibility of being mistaken for a bush.
switches.avoid: Do not make every leaf only hair or ears. Make leaves hide, protect, signal, age, feed, or confuse.

micro_experiments.label: pretends to be a bush badly

switches.principle: Clock hands are limbs, weapons, moustaches, arrows, lies, deadlines, and tiny rulers of panic.
switches.avoid: Do not make every clock hand a limb. Make time itself misbehave.

switches.principle: A button suggests something will happen if pressed. The creature may not know what. This is usually the problem.
switches.avoid: Do not make buttons only eyes or decoration. Make them trigger events, habits, moods, or mistakes.

switches.principle: Pockets create storage, secrets, snacks, theft, mystery, identity, and suspicious bulges.
switches.avoid: Do not make pockets only places to hide things. Make pockets change what the creature wants or does.

switches.principle: A moustache gives an object authority it did not earn, secrets it may not have, and the confidence to explain things incorrectly.
switches.avoid: Do not make moustaches only funny decoration. Let them change social role, attitude, or suspected wisdom.

micro_experiments.label: knows one spell and repeats it

switches.principle: A shadow can reveal what the object thinks it is, what it fears, what it hides, or what it becomes when no one checks.
switches.avoid: Do not make shadows only spooky. Make them reveal identity, memory, ambition, or contradiction.

switches.principle: Strings tie, trail, pull, trip, remember, puppeteer, escape, and make everything look like it has unfinished business.
switches.avoid: Do not make every string a tail. Strings should connect, control, tangle, or reveal.

switches.principle: Holes are mouths, caves, eyes, hiding places, missing pieces, tunnels, mistakes, and entrances for bad ideas.
switches.avoid: Do not make every hole an eye. Holes should hide, swallow, echo, connect, or reveal absence.

switches.principle: Teeth make an object look hungry, serious, defensive, rude, ancient, or unnecessarily prepared.
switches.avoid: Do not make teeth only scary. Make them create appetite, speech, threat, protection, or awkward politeness.

switches.principle: A tail shows balance, mood, speed, history, danger, attachment, and what the creature will knock over next.
switches.avoid: Do not make every tail animal-like. Let tails drag, charge, signal, sweep, write, or betray emotion.

generation_templates.master_image_prompt_template: Create an A5 vertical secret notebook page for Kibookal called CREATURE-MAKER'S NOTEBOOK. The page should look like a found creature-maker's case file, not a worksheet. Warm off-white notebook paper, hand-drawn black ink, blue pencil notes, yellow highlighter marks, orange correction marks, taped scraps, smudges, irregular arrows, crossed-out guesses, small lab stamp, paperclip or punched holes. The page is for ages 9-13: witty, quirky, funny, slightly odd, not babyish. Header: 'CREATURE-MAKER'S NOTEBOOK', 'Case No. {{case_number}}: {{case_title}}', stamp 'ATTACH WONDER METHOD', tiny note 'If found, add one creature and return secretly.' Show one solved case. Started as: {{ordinary_object}}. Draw the ordinary object clearly on the left with suspicious clues: {{suspicious_clues}}. In the middle show a taped scrap called 'WRONG THINGS ATTACHED:' with these odd add-ons: {{wrong_things_attached}}. Add the prompt 'What if it goes there?' On the right or center, draw the final object-creature: {{final_creature_name}}. The original object must remain visible inside the creature. Use simple 2D hand-drawn style, not polished fantasy art. Add funny labels to transformed parts: {{transformed_part_labels}}. Add a crossed-out note: 'First guess: {{first_guess}}' and correction: '{{correction}}' Include a recurring section called 'TODAY'S STRANGE SWITCH: {{strange_switch_feature}}' with principle '{{strange_switch_principle}}' and 4-5 tiny variations: {{strange_switch_micro_experiments}}. Do not make eyes the focus unless the Strange Switch is eyes. Optional lab notes: {{quick_notes_from_lab}}. Bottom section: taped scrap titled 'UNSOLVED CASE: SOMETHING IS HIDING HERE.' Include: 'Choose one object. Add 3 wrong things. Add one Strange Switch somewhere suspicious.' Fields: 'Object spotted:', 'Wrong things attached:', 'Strange Switch I used:', 'It appeared as:'. Include a small irregular sketch space with faint text: 'Draw the first sighting. Not the final masterpiece.' Add corner notes: 'Keep some of the object showing.' and 'The weird bit may go anywhere.' Footer: 'Kibookal rule: Ordinary things are only ordinary until someone stares at them strangely.' Composition should be balanced but not grid-like. Make it feel secret, clever, hand-made and magical.
generation_templates.master_negative_prompt: Do not create a worksheet. Do not use neat rectangular boxes, radio buttons, numbered steps, clean curriculum panels, big empty rectangles, generic stars, trophy language, perfect symmetry, polished corporate vector style, babyish cartoon style, or school assignment feeling. Do not overfill the page with unreadable tiny text. Do not make every creature about eyes. Do not repeat an eye chart unless Today's Strange Switch is eyes. Do not hide the original object inside the creature. Do not make the final creature so polished that a child feels unable to try. Do not use generic praise like Great job, Wow, Awesome, Super cool, or You are a star.

case_generation_prompt.purpose: Generate a new complete case JSON from a starting object.
case_generation_prompt.prompt: Given the ordinary object '{{ordinary_object}}', create a Kibookal Creature-Maker's Notebook case for ages 9-13. Invent a funny object-creature name, 4-6 suspicious clues based on object parts, 6-10 wrong things attached, a final creature drawing description that keeps the object visible, 4-6 transformed part labels, a crossed-out first guess and correction, one Today's Strange Switch that is not eyes unless strongly justified, 4-5 Strange Switch micro-experiments, 3-5 quick lab notes, and one footer rule. Tone must be witty, quirky, dry, odd, and not babyish. Output valid JSON matching the page schema.

prompt_formula.master_prompt: Create one A5 vertical Kibookal Secret Case-File Magazine Notebook page. Use warm aged cream notebook paper, punched holes on the left, taped torn scraps, paperclip, ink splatters, black hand-drawn ink, soft watercolor/colored-pencil wash, blue pencil arrows, yellow highlighter marks, orange/red crossed-out corrections, handmade labels, and rich-but-breathable layout. Keep the style exactly like the approved Creature-Maker notebook reference pages. The page must have one main solved object-creature image, the original object visible, one Started As object, one Wrong Things Attached scrap, one Today's Strange Switch panel, one First Guess crossed out and Correction note, one Quick Notes from the Lab, one Unsolved Case child area, and a Kibookal rule footer. The tone is witty, dry, secretive, odd, not babyish, not classroom worksheet. No glossy vector, no anime, no Pixar/3D, no corporate worksheet, no clean grids.
prompt_formula.negative_prompt: Do not change the style. Do not make it a clean worksheet. No neat rectangular classroom boxes, no radio buttons as dominant layout, no polished fantasy art, no generic cute style, no anime, no 3D/Pixar, no corporate vector, no pure white background, no over-clean typography, no motivational praise, no hidden original object, no generic animal that replaces the object, no overcrowded unreadable text.
